City Council Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

The City Council will consider authorizing the attendance of any Council Member who wishes to attend the National Association of Latino Elected and Appointed Officials (NALEO) 34th Annual Conference in Dallas, TX, from June 22 â€“ 24, 2017.
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the attendance, at the expense of the City, of any Council Member that wishes to attend the NALEO 34th Annual Conference in Dallas, TX, from June 22 - June 24, 2017.

Display of the Vietnamese American Heritage and Freedom Flag with the United States of America Flag Along Valley Blvd. as a Symbol of Freedom and Democracy (Agendized by Councilmember Ly)
The Vietnamese Refugee Community of Los Angeles County is again requesting that the City Council support the Vietnamese American citizens of the Rosemead community by authorizing the display of the Vietnamese American Heritage and Freedom Flag along with the United States of America Flag as a symbol of freedom and democracy on Valley Boulevard from Sunday, April 23, 2017, through Sunday, April 30, 2017. The display of the flags together, side-by-side is consistent with the protocol specified in the United States Flag Code. The flag display will commemorate the fall of Saigon on April 30, 1975.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the request of the Vietnamese Refugee Community of Los Angeles County to display the Vietnamese American Heritage and Freedom Flag side-by-side with the United States of America Flag along Valley Boulevard from April 23, 2017, through April 30, 2017, in accordance with the protocol specified in the United States Flag Code.

One-Year Contract With Auditors
The City of Rosemead currently contracts with a certified public accounting firm, Rogers, Anderson, Malody and Scott, LLP (RAMS) for audit services. The contract expired at the completion of the fiscal year 2015/16 audit. The City Council will consider entering into a one-year contract with RAMS to complete the FY 2016/17 audit to provide stability to the Finance Department during the transition of the new Finance Director. Staff will initiate a competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) for the FY 2017/18 audit. The total contract amount for audit services is $45,510, which is an increase of $628 or 1.4% from their prior contract fees.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the one-year contract with Rogers, Anderson, Malody and Scott, LLP.

The City is anticipating approval from the California Public Utilities Commission within the following month after which construction of the project can begin.
Recommendation: That the City Council:
1.
Approve the plans and specifications for the Jay Imperial Park Project; and
2.
Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with Kasa Construction, Inc., for $1,236,083.00. In addition, authorize an amount of $123,608 (approximately 10%) as a contingency to cover the cost of unforeseen construction expenses.

Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to send a letter opposing SB 231.

She attended this meeting in Washington D.C. on February 8th through February 9th, 2017, Agenda attached. The NLC paid for lodging and flight expenses. However, staff was informed by an NLC representative after the event took place that transportation and meal expenses of $89.36 did not qualify for reimbursement.
Rosemeadâ€™s Municipal Code 2.04.020 states that any Councilmember shall be reimbursed for the necessary and actual expenses incurred in the performance of official duties. All expenses must be verified and documented. The Cityâ€™s Travel Policy #20-02 states that the following expenses require prior Council approval: â€œInternational and out of state travel except to an adjacent state.â€
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the expenses incurred by Mayor Pro Tem Low at the NLC meeting and reimburse her for these expenses.

Public Hearing on General Plan Amendment 16-01, Tentative Tract Map 74095, Planned Development Review 16-01, a Request to Construct a New 21-Unit Residential Planned Development
La Terra Development, LLC, has submitted entitlement applications for the construction of a 21-unit planned development project. The project includes four home designs and three floor plans. The size of the single-family dwelling unit varies from 1,706 square feet to 2,352 square feet with an attached two-car garage. The proposed development will include three private streets, 19,908 square feet of common open space, and 18,287 square feet of private open space. The subject site is located at 1151 San Gabriel Boulevard in a Planned Development (P-D) zone.
This item was presented to the Planning Commission for consideration on March 6, 2017. During the public hearing, Mr. Nguyen, the Director and Administrator of the St. Joseph Retreat Center discussed his concerns regarding the noise and privacy of the retreat house. For this reason, the applicant proposed to modify the steel fence to a block wall. This was supported by the Planning Commission.
Furthermore, the Planning Commission modified and corrected typos in Condition of Approval Numbers 21, 24, and 51. The Planning Commission also added a condition of approval relating to Native American monitoring during project groundbreaking.
Once the public hearing was closed, the Planning Commission voted on a 4-0-0 vote with four ayes, zero noes, and zero abstains. For this reason, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. 17-03, recommending that the City Council adopt Resolution 2017-12 (Attachment â€œAâ€), and the Mitigated Negative Declaration (Attachment â€œBâ€) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (â€œCâ€). The Planning Commission Staff Report, Planning Commission Resolution No. 17-03, and Draft Planning Commission Meeting Minutes are attached as Attachments â€œDâ€, â€œEâ€, and â€œFâ€, respectively.

THE SUBJECT SITE IS LOCATED AT 1152 SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD IN A P-D ZONE (APN: 5275-015-042)

Public Hearing on Design Review 16-02, Conditional Use Permit 16-01, and Zone Change 16-01, a Request to Construct a New Hampton Inn & Suites
Ivar Eagle, LLC, has submitted entitlement applications to construct a new fiveâ€“story Hampton Inn & Suites with 123 guest rooms. The hotel includes a business center, fitness center, meeting room, swimming pool, and snack shop. The project proposes to provide 125 parking spaces. New landscaping will be provided along the northern, western, and southern project boundaries to buffer the project from the adjacent uses. The hotel is proposed to be 67â€™-9â€ in height. The property is located at 8900 Glendon Way (southeast corner of Ivar Avenue and Glendon Way) in a Medium Commercial with a Design Overlay (C-3/D-O) and a Planned Development (P-D) zone.
This item was presented to the Planning Commission for consideration on March 6, 2017. During this meeting, the Planning Commission voiced concerns relating to Condition of Approval Number 48, which requires the applicant to submit a Pedestrian Route Circulation Study to ensure proper measures are taken for pedestrian safety along Glendon Way. Due to the Planning Commissionâ€™s concern, the applicant suggested that they would incorporate a shuttle van for hotel guests to adjacent commercial centers. The Planning Commission was in support of this idea and modified Condition of Approval Number 48, which incorporates shuttle service for hotel guests during the duration of the permit. In addition to this modification, the Planning Commission corrected typos in Condition of Approval Numbers 69 and 70.
At the conclusion of the public hearing, Planning Commissioner Tang stated that he was unable to support the project due to the quality design of the project and its disconnection to the local community. Once the public hearing was closed, the Planning Commission voted on a 2-1-1 vote with two ayes, one no, and one abstain. Under Robertâ€™s Rules of Order, an abstention goes with the majority for purposes of moving the project forward. For this reason, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. 17-04, recommending that the City Council ADOPT Resolution 2017-10 (Attachment â€œAâ€), Ordinance 972 (Attachment â€œBâ€) and the Mitigated Negative Declaration (Attachment â€œCâ€) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (â€œDâ€). The Planning Commission Staff Report, Planning Commission Resolution No. 17-04, and Draft Planning Commission Meeting Minutes are attached as Attachments â€œEâ€, â€œFâ€, and â€œGâ€, respectively.
On March 8, 2017, the applicant informed staff that they have hired a consultant to work on the Pedestrian Route Circulation Study. They are hoping to have this information available at the City Council Meeting.
Recommendation: That the City Council:
1.
Conduct a public hearing and receive public testimony;

THE SUBJECT SITE IS LOCATED AT 8900 GLENDON WAY IN A C-3/D-O AND A P-D ZONES (APN: 5390-018-036)

MATTERS FROM CITY MANAGER & STAFF
A.
Fiscal Year 2017-18 Annual Action Plan for Federally Funded Programs
On February 14, 2017, the City Council conducted a public hearing to receive input on the development of the Cityâ€™s Annual Action Plan for the period of July 1, 2017, - June 30, 2018. Under Federal regulations, no more than 15% of the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) allocation can be used for social service activities. In addition, under the HOME Investment Partnership (HOME) program, at least 15% must be set aside for a Community Housing Development Organization (CHDO). One (1) organization (Southern California Housing Rights Center) that is currently a recipient of CDBG funds made a presentation at the public hearing as well as the one (1) CHDO (Rio Hondo Community Development Corporation) funded under the HOME program.
The Federal government is still working on allocating CDBG and HOME funding awards and has not yet announced the final amounts to each participating community. While the City has not yet been notified of the grant amounts that will be available to meet identified needs within Rosemead for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2017-18, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has warned that it is estimated that Rosemead will receive a decrease in its current $631,009 allocation of CDBG funds and a decrease in its current $218,386 allocation of HOME funds. It will not be certain until Federal notification of awards. In estimating the amount of funding that could be available in the CDBG & HOME program for FY 2017-18, staff included a conservative 5% cut to both programs along with projected carryover funds from FY 2016-17.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Review and finalize the CDBG and HOME funding recommendations under the Cityâ€™s FY 2017-18 Annual Action Plan;
2.
Increase the maximum funding amount under the Grant program from $10,000 to $15,000 per household; and
3.
Increase the maximum funding amount under the First Time Homebuyer program from $70,000 to $95,000 per household.
